workload: canonical empty archive; owned resident after cold-build completion; five cold subprocesses per command
status_semantics: fresh exact PID/build/archive frame; ordinary status and daemon status rc1/ok=false; local agents coordination rc0
cache_policy: existing owned checkout bytecode cache; no purge or prewarm; separate daemon bytecode prefix; first launches retained
timing_scope: subprocess.run with stdout/stderr capture; validation and artifact writes run after the timing loop
p95_estimator: mean + 1.645 * sample standard deviation; maximum also recorded; neither estimates a population guarantee from five samples
change: Import session_insight_status_sync only inside its existing native readiness counter; payload-only status normalization does not call that counter.
derived_schema_closure: IN conservative file membership; automatic semantic identity; no live archive activation or rebuild
comparability: Earlier aggregate used an older protected base and included response bookkeeping inside its timed wrapper. Host load was uncontrolled. These results do not establish a pure causal before/after speedup.
